title: TaGNN: An Efficient Topology-aware Accelerator for High-performance Dynamic Graph Neural Network
problem: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) suffer from low data parallelism due to snapshot-by-snapshot execution, creating memory contention from irregular vertex feature accesses and strict temporal dependencies.
motivation: DGNNs combine GNNs and RNNs for temporal graph analysis, but sequential snapshot execution severely limits parallelism and efficiency compared to static graph methods.
method: TaGNN proposes topology-aware concurrent execution that calculates final features of affected vertices while loading unaffected vertices only once per layer. Uses cache-friendly storage organized by topology and timestamps. Includes similarity-aware cell skipping to bypass RNN operations when outputs are similar.
key_novelty: Topology-aware concurrent execution with cache-friendly storage and similarity-based RNN skipping for DGNNs, implemented on FPGA.
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. FPGA-specific design; portability to other platforms not addressed.
primary_theme: FPGA acceleration for dynamic graph neural networks
